	got := run("--base", "main")
	if got.BaseRef != "main" || got.BaseCommit != branchPoint || got.ChangedFiles != 1 ||
		len(got.Items) != 1 || got.Items[0].Path != "README.md" || got.Items[0].Reasons[0].Target != "Orders" {
		t.Fatalf("--base main = %+v; want README.md's Orders section against the branch point %s", got, branchPoint)
	}
}
EOF

- Added nightly LoCoMo benchmark CI for the entire-graph arm, authenticated via OIDC with no stored credentials.
- Added a `NOTICES` file to every release archive, covering the third-party parser sources and Go modules statically linked into the binary.

- Added experimental `X-entire-graph:MENTIONS` and `X-entire-graph:LINKS_TO` relations (full profile): a Markdown section links to the code symbols and repository files it names in inline code, and to the files and sections it links to, so a change can be traced to the docs that describe it. `neighbors` and `snapshot-query` now match relation types case-insensitively, which extension types need.

-- Added `graph docs`, which lists the Markdown sections a working-tree change probably made stale (they name a changed or removed symbol, link to a changed section, or usually change with a changed code file), and told agents in the generated guide to run it and update those sections in the same change.

lines: - Added a `NOTICES` file to every release archive, covering the third-party parser sources and Go modules statically linked into the binary.

- Added experimental `X-entire-graph:MENTIONS` and `X-entire-graph:LINKS_TO` relations (full profile): a Markdown section links to the code symbols and repository files it names in inline code, and to the files and sections it links to, so a change can be traced to the docs that describe it. `neighbors` and `snapshot-query` now match relation types case-insensitively, which extension types need.

- Added `graph docs`, which lists the Markdown sections a working-tree change probably made stale (they name a changed or removed symbol, link to a changed section, or usually change with a changed code file), and told agents in the generated guide to run it and update those sections in the same change. `--base <ref>` covers a branch's commits as well, comparing from the merge base like `git diff <ref>...HEAD`.

| `agent-guide` | Prints the operating guide `init-agents` installs, for inspection or piping elsewhere. |

#!/bin/sh
# Walks `entire graph docs` through a throwaway repo: a body change, a removed
# function, an edited section that another doc links to, and then the doc fixes.
#
#   mise run build && sh scripts/demo-docs.sh [path/to/entire-graph]
set -eu

work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
repo=$work/shop

export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=demo GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=demo@example.com

package billing

type Invoice struct {
	Lines []float64
}

func TotalWithTax(inv Invoice, rate float64) float64 {
	total := 0.0
	for _, line := range inv.Lines {
		total += line
	}
	return total * (1 + rate)
}

}

content.text:
Both pieces are built, as two new PRs stacked on #6:
- **[PR #7](https://github.com/JesseVent/entire-graph/pull/7), `docs --base`:** branch support, so a trail's runners can check stale docs.
- **[PR #8](https://github.com/JesseVent/entire-graph/pull/8), `docs init`:** the starting point for new repos, plus the Doc staleness runner.

The full test suite, `gofmt`, `go vet`, the notices check and the status-line tests all pass. The only thing not yet confirmed is the new runner reporting a score on a live trail; I'm watching for that now.

**PR #7: `docs --base <ref>`.** `docs` previously only saw uncommitted edits. With `--base` it starts from where the branch split off (like `git diff <ref>...HEAD`), so a branch's commits are covered too. The snapshot cache is keyed by git tree, so I threaded the base revision through the cache lookup as well as the build; without that, a cache hit would have reported HEAD.

Two changes to output:
- **Parse failures:** this PR also tightens my fix for the runner's earlier finding (#6). Text output now mentions only parse failures that could hide a doc: ones in a changed file or a Markdown file. Before, every run on this repo opened with failures in vendored C headers.
- **Historical docs:** archived plans and changelogs are now left out of the list, since they record the past. Running `docs` on its own change kept turning up hits in `docs/archive/`.

**PR #8: `docs init` and the runner.** One run of `entire graph docs init`:
- **Audits existing drift:** links to docs or headings that don't exist, file paths in backticks that git history shows were deleted or moved, and `pkg.Name`-style names whose package no longer has that member.
- **Reports coverage:** how many doc sections name code, and which heavily used code directories no doc mentions.
- **Adds the runner:** it writes `.entire/runners/trail-docs.json`, a Doc staleness runner, if `.entire/runners/` already exists. It never overwrites an existing file. In a repo with no runners it tells you to run `entire runner setup` first.

The runner scores each trail as a percentage, like Drift: the share of doc sections pointing at the branch's changes that the branch didn't update, lower being better. It names up to three of them. It uses `entire graph docs --base` if that's installed in the runner's environment, builds the binary from source if Go is available, and otherwise falls back to checking the diff against the docs by hand.

**Accuracy on this repo:**
- **First run:** 197 problems reported, none of them real drift. Most were `go.mod` read as a package name, a test fixture's `Router` type, and deleted benchmark files named in archived plans. The two that looked real were example paths, such as `.github/workflows/ci.yml` given as an illustration.
- **After the fixes:** it reports 0. The key rule is that a missing path only counts if the repo really did have it once.
- **Recall check:** I moved `internal/sem/health.go` on a scratch branch, and the audit flagged exactly the one doc line that still named it.

Running `docs` on its own changes found real drift twice: the `CLAUDE.md` Architecture row was out of date both times, and I updated it in each PR.

**Differences from the plan:**
- **`docs/agents.md`:** I didn't add the planned mention there, because it only covers what `init-agents` writes. `docs init` is in the command reference's "Set up" table instead.
- **Trail #6:** getting the new runner onto its branch means merging #7 and #8 into it, which is your call. Trail #9, which Entire opened for PR #8, already has the runner file on its branch, so I'm watching that one instead. If the score doesn't show up there, runners probably load from `main`, and it will appear once the stack is merged.

**To merge:** #6, then #7, then #8, with merge commits as before. Each PR targets the one before it.

Trail #5 still needs closing from its web page.
